name: Tengger Javanese, 'bahasa Jawa dialek Tengger'
confidence_why: The one phonological description of Tengger Javanese, Soedjito et al. 1984, states that stress can fall on any syllable of a word (their example /saulan/) without changing its meaning, and the other available works (Sunoto et al. 1990, Andayani 2018, Conners 2006-2010) are silent on stress, so the record rests on a single first-hand source with nothing against it.

catalog_quote: 3.6 Fonem Suprasegmental. Dalam dialek Tengger tidak terdapat fonem suprasegmental. Perbedaan tekanan, nada, panjang-pendek, dan jeda tidak berfungsi membedakan makna suatu kata. Kata /saulan/ misalnya, baik diucapkan [saʔulan] dengan tekanan pada suku /sa-/ maupun diucapkan [saulan] dengan tekanan pada suku /u-/ atau pada suku /-lan/ tidak berbeda maknanya. [Translation: 3.6 Suprasegmental phonemes. In the Tengger dialect there are no suprasegmental phonemes. Differences of stress, pitch, length and juncture do not function to distinguish the meaning of a word. The word /saulan/, for example, whether pronounced [saʔulan] with stress on the syllable /sa-/ or pronounced [saulan] with stress on the syllable /u-/ or on the syllable /-lan/, does not differ in meaning.]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is not phonemic in Tengger Javanese and, per the authors' example, may fall on any syllable of a word (initial, medial or final) without change of meaning; the grammar gives no default or preferred stress position and otherwise treats stress only as an ingredient of sentence intonation contours (citation form of a disyllable transcribed /2 1 #/, i.e. falling pitch). Read here as 'no (fixed) word stress per source'; strictly it is a non-contrastiveness statement with free placement rather than an explicit denial of phonetic prominence.
new_statements.domain_note: Word level (isolated words, meaning contrast). Section 5.2.2 adds that stress, pitch and pause belong to sentence-level intonation patterns: tuku 'buy' in isolation /2 1 #/, but tuku pitik 'buy a chicken' /2 2 2 1 #/. Data from Ngadisari (Sukapura, Probolinggo), Wonotoro and Ngadas villages, fieldwork 1980/81.
new_statements.identity_note: The 1984 Pusat Bahasa study describes 'bahasa Jawa dialek Tengger' as spoken in the Tengger highlands of Probolinggo, Pasuruan, Malang and Lumajang regencies, with sample villages Ngadisari (Sukapura), Wonotoro and Ngadas; this is the same variety as Glottolog teng1272 / ISO tes (Conners' 'Tengger Javanese', Smith-Hefner's 'Cara Tengger'). Glottolog and Conners treat it as a Javanese dialect; Ethnologue lists it as a separate language.

sources.note: Ch. III Fonologi, section 3.6 'Fonem Suprasegmental' (p.53): the Tengger dialect has no suprasegmental phonemes; differences of stress, pitch, length and juncture do not distinguish word meaning; e.g. /saulan/ means the same whether stressed on /sa-/, /u-/ or /-lan/. Section 5.2.2 (p.140) treats stress, pitch and pause only as components of sentence intonation patterns (citation form tuku = /2 1 #/, in phrase tuku pitik = /2 2 2 1 #/). No statement of a default stress position.
